items.title: Register the 7 missing Experience-Layer/recall commands in PROCESS_FACT_REGISTRY
items.context: In packages/main/src/core/process-fact-registry.ts (PROCESS_FACT_REGISTRY array ~line 871), add entries for playbook_approve, playbook_diff, playbook_propose, playbook_reject, recall, signature_registry_list, signature_registry_set. Mirror the existing entry shape (name/level/category/owner/rationale, plus gateConsumer where a gate reads the fact) seen in process-fact-levels.ts (~lines 47-49) and the existing registry entries. Read each command's handler to classify accurately: read-only queries (signature_registry_list, playbook_diff, recall if read-only) get low levels (L0/L1, category reflecting their domain); mutating commands (playbook_approve/reject/propose, signature_registry_set) get the level/category matching how they mutate + any gateConsumer. Do NOT change command behavior. Verify: `npm run test:process-fact-contract` no longer reports 'MAIN_TOOLS command missing from PROCESS_FACT_REGISTRY' for these 7.
items.userSees: `npm run test:process-fact-contract` no longer lists playbook_*/signature_registry_*/recall as missing from PROCESS_FACT_REGISTRY; each appears with an accurate level/category/owner.

happy.desc: After registering the 7 commands in PROCESS_FACT_LEVELS and rebuilding, npm run test:process-fact-contract reports NO `MAIN_TOOLS command ... missing from PROCESS_FACT_REGISTRY` lines and NO `MAIN_TOOLS command(s) missing from registry` line for the 7 commands

edge.desc: Each of the 7 commands appears in the registry dump with an accurate level/category/owner matching its handler behavior (3 read-only L0, 4 mutating L2, none gate-consumed) — verified by inspecting the contract registry dump output

adversarial.desc: No command behavior change: git diff touches only process-fact-levels.ts (and not handlers/cli-engine.ts); a mutating command is not falsely registered as read-only and vice versa

verificationEvidence.note: After adding 7 entries to PROCESS_FACT_LEVELS + npm --prefix packages/main run build (BUILD_EXIT=0), node scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs exits 0; grep -E "MAIN_TOOLS command|missing from registry" /tmp/pfc-chk001.log returns rc=1 (no matches) — no missing-command line mentions playbook_*/signature_registry_*/recall.

Registry dump lists all 7 with accurate levels/owners: signature_registry_list [L0] handlers/signature-registry, playbook_diff [L0] handlers/playbook, recall [L0] handlers/recall (3 read-only); signature_registry_set [L2] handlers/signature-registry, playbook_propose/playbook_approve/playbook_reject [L2] handlers/playbook (4 mutating). None has gateConsumer — verified against each handler (lists/renders are read-only; .lattice/learning writes have no gate reader).

No command behavior change: commit 3ded509e9 git show --stat shows ONLY packages/main/src/core/process-fact-levels.ts (1 file, +7 lines); no handlers/* or cli-engine.ts change. Levels match handler reality (read-only listers/renders/recall = L0; .lattice/learning mutators = L2); no read-only command falsely registered as mutating or vice versa.

items.title: Reconcile DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS so recall/signature_registry_*/playbook_* phase drift is resolved, and confirm the whole contract is GREEN
items.context: The contract also reports DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS phase allowlist drift for patterns recall / signature_registry_* / playbook_* across PLAN/REVIEW/TEST. In config.ts (DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS), reconcile the phase allowlists so they agree with the registry/command-policy for these commands (add them to the phases where they are legitimately allowed; the contract enforces DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS ⊆ command-policy allowedPhases — keep that safe direction). Honor the Handler Encoding Convention if any consumed field has constraints. Then run `npm run test:process-fact-contract` and confirm it EXITS 0 (green) end-to-end — the gate does not run this guard today, so this explicit run is the verification of record. Capture the green output as evidence.
items.userSees: `npm run test:process-fact-contract` exits 0 with no drift/missing lines — the process-fact invariant is green on the story branch; the green transcript is the real-machine evidence.

happy.desc: npm run test:process-fact-contract exits 0 end-to-end — NO `Process fact contract failed:` block, NO `DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS phase allowlist drift` lines (the 21 drift lines from baseline are gone)

edge.desc: DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS stays a subset of command-policy allowedPhases (safe direction preserved); if config.ts was edited at all, no phase allowlist was widened beyond what policy permits

adversarial.desc: The contract guard is satisfied honestly (entries registered), not by relaxing/ignoring the 7 commands; npx tsc still exits 0 (no type regression)
